about: Authored query pairs on Chinook for tools/sample_db_bench.py. label: 'equivalent' or 'different' under the declared keys minus 'drop' (not_null:T.c, pk:T, fk:T.c). A 'different' pair carries a witness: 'real' (the two queries already differ on the Chinook data) or a small database (missing columns are completed with legal values) that satisfies the remaining declarations and separates them. 'sibling' names the pair it negates.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: Track.MediaTypeId is NOT NULL and references MediaType's key: every track joins exactly one media type
pairs.left: SELECT t.TrackId, t.Name FROM Track AS t JOIN MediaType AS m ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId
pairs.right: SELECT TrackId, Name FROM Track

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Track.AlbumId may be NULL: such a track joins no album
pairs.left: SELECT t.TrackId, t.Name FROM Track AS t JOIN Album AS a ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId
pairs.right: SELECT TrackId, Name FROM Track

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key a track may name a media type that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT t.TrackId, t.Name FROM Track AS t JOIN MediaType AS m ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId
pairs.right: SELECT TrackId, Name FROM Track

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without MediaType's key two media types may share an id, and the join repeats the track
pairs.left: SELECT t.TrackId, t.Name FROM Track AS t JOIN MediaType AS m ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId
pairs.right: SELECT TrackId, Name FROM Track

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a LEFT JOIN to Employee on its key neither drops nor repeats a customer, and no Employee column is read
pairs.left: SELECT c.CustomerId, c.LastName FROM Customer AS c LEFT JOIN Employee AS e ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId
pairs.right: SELECT CustomerId, LastName FROM Customer

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Invoice.CustomerId is no key: a customer with two invoices appears twice
pairs.left: SELECT c.CustomerId, c.LastName FROM Customer AS c LEFT JOIN Invoice AS i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
pairs.right: SELECT CustomerId, LastName FROM Customer

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: TrackId is the key, so the rows are already distinct
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT TrackId, Name FROM Track
pairs.right: SELECT TrackId, Name FROM Track

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: many tracks share an album
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT AlbumId FROM Track
pairs.right: SELECT AlbumId FROM Track

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the key two tracks may be the same row
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT TrackId, Name FROM Track
pairs.right: SELECT TrackId, Name FROM Track

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: IN over a subquery is a semi-join, as EXISTS is
pairs.left: SELECT CustomerId FROM Customer WHERE CustomerId IN (SELECT CustomerId FROM Invoice WHERE Total > 20)
pairs.right: SELECT c.CustomerId FROM Customer AS c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Invoice AS i WHERE i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId AND i.Total > 20)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a join repeats a customer once per matching invoice; IN does not
pairs.left: SELECT c.CustomerId FROM Customer AS c JOIN Invoice AS i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId WHERE i.Total > 5
pairs.right: SELECT CustomerId FROM Customer WHERE CustomerId IN (SELECT CustomerId FROM Invoice WHERE Total > 5)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: both TrackId columns are NOT NULL, so NOT IN and NOT EXISTS agree
pairs.left: SELECT TrackId FROM Track WHERE TrackId NOT IN (SELECT TrackId FROM InvoiceLine)
pairs.right: SELECT t.TrackId FROM Track AS t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM InvoiceLine AS il WHERE il.TrackId = t.TrackId)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Track.Composer holds NULLs, so NOT IN returns no row while NOT EXISTS returns many
pairs.left: SELECT ArtistId FROM Artist WHERE Name NOT IN (SELECT Composer FROM Track)
pairs.right: SELECT a.ArtistId FROM Artist AS a WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Track AS t WHERE t.Composer = a.Name)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: once InvoiceLine.TrackId may be NULL, one NULL line empties the NOT IN result
pairs.left: SELECT TrackId FROM Track WHERE TrackId NOT IN (SELECT TrackId FROM InvoiceLine)
pairs.right: SELECT t.TrackId FROM Track AS t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM InvoiceLine AS il WHERE il.TrackId = t.TrackId)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: Customer.Email is NOT NULL, so COUNT(Email) counts every row
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(Email) FROM Customer
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Customer

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Customer.Company is NULL for most customers
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(Company) FROM Customer
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Customer

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: AlbumId is Album's key, so Title and ArtistId are fixed within a group: grouping by them too changes nothing
pairs.left: SELECT al.AlbumId, al.Title, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Album AS al JOIN Track AS t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId GROUP BY al.AlbumId, al.Title, al.ArtistId
pairs.right: SELECT al.AlbumId, al.Title, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Album AS al JOIN Track AS t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId GROUP BY al.AlbumId, al.Title

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: an album's tracks may have several genres, which splits its group
pairs.left: SELECT t.AlbumId, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Track AS t GROUP BY t.AlbumId, t.GenreId
pairs.right: SELECT t.AlbumId, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Track AS t GROUP BY t.AlbumId

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: UNION DISTINCT removes the repeated countries UNION ALL keeps
pairs.left: SELECT Country FROM Customer UNION ALL SELECT Country FROM Employee
pairs.right: SELECT Country FROM Customer UNION DISTINCT SELECT Country FROM Employee

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: Milliseconds is NOT NULL, so every track satisfies exactly one of the two filters
pairs.left: SELECT TrackId FROM Track WHERE Milliseconds > 300000 UNION ALL SELECT TrackId FROM Track WHERE Milliseconds <= 300000
pairs.right: SELECT TrackId FROM Track

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Track.Bytes may be NULL: such a track satisfies neither filter
pairs.left: SELECT TrackId FROM Track WHERE Bytes > 1000000 UNION ALL SELECT TrackId FROM Track WHERE Bytes <= 1000000
pairs.right: SELECT TrackId FROM Track

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the WHERE condition rejects the NULL-extended rows of the LEFT JOIN
pairs.left: SELECT c.CustomerId, e.LastName FROM Customer AS c LEFT JOIN Employee AS e ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId WHERE e.Title = 'Sales Support Agent'
pairs.right: SELECT c.CustomerId, e.LastName FROM Customer AS c JOIN Employee AS e ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId WHERE e.Title = 'Sales Support Agent'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: e.Title IS NULL accepts the NULL-extended row of a customer without a support rep
pairs.left: SELECT c.CustomerId, e.LastName FROM Customer AS c LEFT JOIN Employee AS e ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId WHERE e.Title IS NULL OR e.Title = 'Sales Support Agent'
pairs.right: SELECT c.CustomerId, e.LastName FROM Customer AS c JOIN Employee AS e ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId WHERE e.Title IS NULL OR e.Title = 'Sales Support Agent'

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a HAVING condition on the grouping column can filter the rows before grouping
pairs.left: SELECT GenreId, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Track GROUP BY GenreId HAVING GenreId > 5
pairs.right: SELECT GenreId, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Track WHERE GenreId > 5 GROUP BY GenreId

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a genre with no long track is missing on the left and counted 0 on the right
pairs.left: SELECT GenreId, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Track WHERE Milliseconds > 200000 GROUP BY GenreId
pairs.right: SELECT GenreId, COUNTIF(Milliseconds > 200000) AS n FROM Track GROUP BY GenreId

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a filter on the PARTITION BY column keeps or drops whole partitions, so it can run before the window
pairs.left: SELECT TrackId, AlbumId, r FROM (SELECT TrackId, AlbumId, Milliseconds, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY AlbumId ORDER BY Milliseconds) AS r FROM Track) WHERE AlbumId = 5
pairs.right: SELECT TrackId, AlbumId, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY AlbumId ORDER BY Milliseconds) AS r FROM Track WHERE AlbumId = 5

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: filtering on Milliseconds first removes rows the ranking counted
pairs.left: SELECT TrackId, AlbumId, r FROM (SELECT TrackId, AlbumId, Milliseconds, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY AlbumId ORDER BY Milliseconds) AS r FROM Track) WHERE Milliseconds > 300000
pairs.right: SELECT TrackId, AlbumId, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY AlbumId ORDER BY Milliseconds) AS r FROM Track WHERE Milliseconds > 300000

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: Track.GenreId references Genre's key: a track joins one genre exactly when GenreId is not NULL
pairs.left: SELECT t.TrackId FROM Track AS t JOIN Genre AS g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
pairs.right: SELECT TrackId FROM Track WHERE GenreId IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key a track may name a genre that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT t.TrackId FROM Track AS t JOIN Genre AS g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
pairs.right: SELECT TrackId FROM Track WHERE GenreId IS NOT NULL
